articleTitle: Novel Square Wave Jamming Strategy for Countering Sequential Lobing Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative jamming strategy designed to improve the effectiveness of square wave jamming (SWJ) against sequential lobing radars (SLRs). The proposed method incorporates phase reversal into the traditional SWJ technique to exploit the vulnerabilities inherent in angular tracking loops. This results in significant angular errors in the radar’s tracking system, potentially causing the radar to lose track of targets when they move through the sidelobe regions of its antenna beams. Notably, the new strategy reduces the jamming-to-signal-ratio (JSR) required to induce track loss compared to conventional SWJ methods, demonstrating a notable improvement of approximately 3 dB in the required JSR. These results underscore the enhanced effectiveness of the proposed approach in addressing SLR vulnerabilities to SWJ.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of 2x2 MIMO Antennas with Metasurface Structure for Mitigating Mutual Coupling in 5G MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of different metasurface structures in a $2 \times 2$ MIMO antenna system. Three unit cells were designed and analyzed using dispersion diagram analysis to achieve resonance of surface wave propagation at 3.5 GHz. The unit cells were arranged in an array to observe their effect on reducing mutual coupling. Each unit cell demonstrated varying levels of optimal mutual coupling reduction at different antenna spacings. All three unit cells achieved mutual coupling reductions of up to 40 dB, with the closest antenna spacing at 1.06 wavelengths. Other performance aspects, such as the Envelope Correlation Coefficient and diversity gain, were also studied.

articleTitle: Design of Elliptical Patch and Half-Circular Ground Microstrip Antenna with CPW-Fed for Chamber Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study designed an elliptical patch microstrip antenna with CPW-Fed to test wave-absorbing materials on the inner chamber walls at a wideband frequency. To achieve the required frequency range, calculations were performed for the dimensions of the patch and the impedance line. The antenna has dimensions of $60 \times 62 \mathrm{~mm}$ and uses FR-4 material with a substrate thickness of 1.6 mm, a copper thickness of 0.035 mm, and a relative permittivity of 4.3. The antenna was initially designed with a rectangular ground, but testing results showed limited bandwidth. To improve the performance, the ground was modified into a half-circular, and the curvature of the ground was optimized. The best results were achieved with a curvature ground of 14 mm and the antenna operating frequency ranging from 1.81 GHz to 18 GHz, with a minimum peak value at -49 dB. The radiation pattern measured in the elevation angle at a theta 0 degrees produced a maximum radiation of $\mathbf{- 1 3. 6} \mathrm{dBi}$ parallel to the antenna plane, with a relatively large half-power beamwidth (HPBW). The antenna gain is in the range of $\mathbf{2. 5}$ to 5 dBi. Although the antenna gain is relatively low, the antennas are suitable for testing absorbing materials on the inner chamber walls, considering the wide bandwidth aspect and the medium chamber size.

articleTitle: Measurement of pH Water Based on Sensor, Arduino and Solar Cell in Laser Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: We connected $\mathbf{p H}$ sensor and solar cell into Arduino Board to control data transmission via red laser communication or popular known as visible light communication (VLC). The sensor was calibrated through pH water solution measurement compared with conventional $\mathbf{p H}$ Meter. This sensor collected and then modulated $\mathbf{p H}$ data in Arduino to be sent via laser beam. The beam is captured by solar cell which acts as a photodetector in receiver. The received data will be demodulated in Arduino to be displayed in serial monitor to observe the communication performance. As the result, the link distance of laser communication can reach 35 m using 1-PWM and 15 m using 2-PWM, in freespace environment. When the transmission channel was changed into water environment, the link distance will decrease severely. The prototype output of this work will be a future self-powered modem for water surface and underwater monitoring system.

articleTitle: Unstructured Road Detection using a Superpixel-Based Image Segmentation Clustering for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In real-world applications, such as autonomous driving, image-based road recognition is both critical and challenging. This research paper focuses on detecting unstructured roads using an enhanced feature-based method. The algorithm we propose uses the image segmentation method. The two best methods, called K-means and Fuzzy C-means, are being selected, and to improve the result of road detection, we combine with Superpixel Linear Iterative Clustering (SLIC) that converts pixels into superpixels that accurately depict the structure of the objects in the picture. According to the experimental findings, the most effective proposed algorithm for detecting potholes and road prediction for unstructured roads is the modified K -Means algorithm, which employs superpixels (SP-Kmeans) as clustering objects instead of pixels since it provides the maximum accuracy, reaching an average accuracy of 92.47 percent.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Suppression by Using Aluminium and Copper Shield in UAV Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Crosstalk is a significant concern in the design of cabling systems for UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles). Some factors such as, cable length, type, spacing between cables, and cable layout must be carefully considered to mitigate electromagnetic interference. This study examines various types of cables and the effect of spacing between cables, as well as the effect of cable shields using aluminum and copper to see their effectiveness in reducing crosstalk. Crosstalk levels were measured at both the near end (NEXT) and far end (FEXT) of the cables through CST Cable simulations in the frequency range of 1 to 900 MHz. Results indicate that increased spacing between cables can reduces crosstalk, with higher levels observed at the NEXT compared to the FEXT. Additionally, twisting cables can reduce NEXT crosstalk by up to 19 dBv at a 0 cm distance from the source cable. Furthermore, shielded cables significantly reduce crosstalk above frequency 300 MHz, with copper foil providing a 10 dBv reduction compared to unshielded cables and a 2 dBv reduction over aluminum foil.

articleTitle: Robust Features with Convolutional Autoencoder Speech Command Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Today, deep learning (DL) has proven to be a prominent method in many recognition tasks. However, deep learning-based Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) has degraded performance when dealing with noisy data. In this study, we investigate the effectiveness of DL architectures using the autoencoder convolutional neural network (AECNN) combined with traditional feature extraction methods such as Mel-Filter Bank (MFB), Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and Log Mel-Filter Bank (LMFB) to generate robust features for speech command recognition. We implement RMSprop as an optimizer to get optimal models. Based on our experiment results, we found that MFB features perform best in both clean and noisy conditions.

articleTitle: Single Parity Check Network Coding Based on Iterative Spatial Demapper
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper proposes a network coding scheme based on single parity check (SPC-NC) with structure exploiting iterative spatial demapper (ISM) to reduce time-slots in relay-assisted multi-source to single-destination wireless communications. This paper uses ISM at the destination to separate the merged information from two users, a challenging task akin to solving equations with two variables. Repetition codes and relays are used for error protection and signal quality improvement, to achieve order-2 diversity. A series of computer simulations confirm that SPC-NC can effectively combine two users into a single time-slot using ISM, reducing overall time-slots. The results shows that SPC-NC with amplify-and-forward (AF) relays supports simultaneous transmission of two users, offering good performance by resembling SPC codes and providing additional gain. The findings aim to advance future network coding development.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control in Automatic Train Operation (ATO) during Unplanned Event
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Automatic Train Operation (ATO) systems have become essential in urban rail networks with the aim of minimizing human error, improving punctuality, and optimizing energy consumption. However, unplanned incidents, such as post-automatic train protection (ATP) or driver interventions, reduce the performance of the designed ATO. This study aims to evaluate the ability of the optimal quadratic control strategy to deal with ATO during unplanned events, including driver intervention. By simulating various scenarios and analyzing key performance indicators, this research provides information on the robustness, adaptability, and overall contribution of the strategy to the reliability of ATO systems. The findings inform improvements in control algorithms, ultimately improving the resilience and efficiency of urban rail systems.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties Observation of Polymer-Based Hygroelectric Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Hygroelectric Generator (HEG) generates electricity from the air by absorbing water molecules. In this research, the fabrication of HEG devices with self-healable properties has been successfully developed based on Poly(2-acrylamido-2-methyl-1-propanesulfonic acid (PAMPSA) polymer composite. Electrical property was observed by measuring the output voltage in varied relative humidity (RH). Testing the self-healing properties was performed by monitoring the output voltage when cutting the sample device. The results of testing electrical hygroelectric properties at varying relative humidity (RH) at 30%, 50% and 80% produce average output voltages of $0.001 \mathrm{~V}, 0.112 \mathrm{~V}$ and 0.304 V, respectively. The result of the self-healing test was seen from the regenerating voltage after the sample was spontaneously reconnected. These findings suggest that PAMPSA-based HEG devices have considerable potential for future applications in sustainable energy harvesting from ambient humidity.

articleTitle: Rectangular Resonator with Radial Stubs Bandpass Filter at 3 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a bandpass filter using a microstrip with an open loop resonator, both simulated and realized. The design uses a rectangular resonator with radial stubs. This paper discusses a symmetrical rectangular resonator shape with a variation in the feeder section. The bandpass is designed to work at S-Band frequencies, with a center frequency of 3 GHz. The design, simulation, and realization of this bandpass filter use NPC-H220A substrate material with a dielectric constant ($\varepsilon_{r}$) of 2.18, and the thickness of this substrate is $\mathbf{1. 2 ~ m m}$. The objective of designing this bandpass filter is to obtain several response parameters, including insertion loss, return loss, and a narrow bandwidth. The design, simulation, and realization of this filter are presented with key response parameters, including a return loss of 23.709 dB, an insertion loss of 0.666 dB, and a resulting bandwidth of 130 MHz at 3 GHz, along with the realization of the bandpass filter. The complete results will be presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Multi-Spectral-Based Imaging with Application to Millimeter Wave Imaging at W-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Frequency dependency of the radar cross-section of targets is an interesting topic with numerous applications. In this paper, we present a novel technique at the signal processing level to create high-resolution radar images that can display the behavior of the radar cross-section of targets over the frequency band upon which the imagery system operates. The proposed method is based on partitioning the entire operational bandwidth into 3 sub-bands. The main application of the proposed approach is material characterization.We present the experimental results based on the data collected from our wide-band custom-built Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar which operates at W-band with 33 GHz bandwidth. From the experimental results, it is evident that targets such as a spherical reflector exhibits the same response over the entire bandwidth while for frequency-selective materials, the output of each sub-band yields a different value for the estimated radar cross-section.

articleTitle: L5-Pelvic Junction Compression Force and Shear Force Based on IMU Sensors and Biomechanical Analysis during Oil Palm Harvesting-Push Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Oil palm harvesting presents a considerable risk for the development of musculoskeletal disorder (MSDs), particularly low back pain (LBP). The use of IMU sensors is crucial for providing feedback to improve manual material handling techniques, which can mitigate LBP risk. This study aims to investigate oil palm harvesting techniques using IMU sensors combined with biomechanical analysis to identify and mitigate potential risks associated with LBP. The research focused primarily on biomechanical criteria, specifically peak compression force and shear force, observed in 3 experienced harvesters using push technique. These results highlight the necessity for developing enhanced harvesting techniques to lower the risk of LBP.

articleTitle: Enhanced Recognition of Hand-Drawn Circuit Components Using Fast R-CNN and Faster R-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: There has been a growing interest in digitizing hand drawn circuits. The first step in this regard would be to identify the different components drawn in the circuit. While many approaches exist in literature, they have been performed for cases where the number of components is minimal. In this paper, we propose two approaches for identifying hand drawn electronic circuit components. The first approach makes use of Fast Region Based Convolutional Neural Network (Fast R-CNN) for identification where as the second approach utilises Faster Region Based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN). For experimentation purpose, we have created a dataset of 22 electronic components such as resistors, inductors, transistors and some basic gates which are hand drawn and comprising of 4235 images in total. The experiments show that the Faster R-CNN outperforms Fast R-CNN by $\mathbf{1. 5 \%}$.

articleTitle: Design of Volumetric Magnetic Induction Tomography (VMIT) System Using COMSOL Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Magnetic Induction Tomography (MIT) is a low-resolution imaging technique used to reconstruct the magnetic permeability distribution of an object. COMSOL Simulation of VMIT (Volumetric Magnetic Induction Tomography) system has been developed by using 8 coils as transmitter and 8 coils as receiver. The existence of sine excitation signal in the transmitter coil cause magnetic field changing, it causing emf at the receiver coil. The magnitude of the magnetic field induction is also influenced by the permeability of the medium between the transmitter and receiver coils. COMSOL and MATLAB simulation of VMIT 8 coil systems indicate that, by using ILBP algorithms, ball-shaped object with ferromagnetic materials (iron) can be reconstructed to produce a similar image. The sensitivity matrix significantly influences image reconstruction in MIT, leading to distorted elliptical images of objects, particularly when positioned at the top center, as the matrix shows homogeneity mainly in the middle area.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an E-Textile SSPP-Based Low-Pass Filter for Advanced Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an electronic textile (e-textile) low-pass filter (LPF) based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons (SSPPs), achieving a cutoff frequency of 6.47 GHz for advanced wearable applications. The proposed filter comprises m-shaped unit cells designed to be patterned on the top side of a denim substrate, complemented by a complete ground plane on the back side. The dimensions of the filter are $2.15 \lambda_{0} \times 0.539 \lambda_{0} \times 0.034 \lambda_{0}$, where $\lambda_{0}$ is the wavelength corresponding to the cutoff frequency. Simulation results reveal a passband frequency range extending from 0 GHz to 6.47 GHz, with a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 6.47 GHz and a stopband attenuation of -45 dB at 6.90 GHz. The filter demonstrates low insertion loss within the passband, with a maximum value of just 0.8 dB. Finally, the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) values of $0.0268 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{kg}$ and 0.0125 $\mathrm{W} / \mathrm{kg}$ for both the 1 g and 10 g standards, respectively indicate compliance with safety regulations, affirming its suitability for wearable applications on the human body. The e-textile design and SAR analysis ensure that the filter remains both flexible and comfortable, making it well-suited for integration into smart clothing and other wearable devices.

articleTitle: Exploration of In2S3 as an Electron Transport Layer for All-Inorganic CsPbBr3 Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate the fabrication of planar-based CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> perovskite solar cells with the use of $\mathrm{In}_{2} \mathrm{~S}_{3}$ as an electron transport layer (ETL) fabricated by chemical bath deposition. CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films were fabricated by multi-step spin coating of PbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and CsBr ink, respectively, followed by annealing in air at $250^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ for 30 min followed by deposition of a carbon-based electrode. The device showed an efficiency of $0.7 \%\left(J_{s c}=1.3 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}, \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{oc}}=1.165 \mathrm{~V} F \mathrm{FF}=47 \%\right.$), which was higher than that of the device without an ETL with an efficiency of $0.4 \%\left(J_{\mathrm{sc}}=1.9 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}, \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{oc}}=0.685 \mathrm{~V} \mathrm{FF}=\right.$ 32%). A relatively small grain sizes of the CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> film growth in the $\mathbf{I n}_{2} \mathrm{~S}_{3}$ layer ($\sim \mathbf{5 0 0} \mathbf{~ n m}$) was thought to be responsible for the relatively low efficiency of the device compared to that of using a conventional TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer as the ETL layer.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of ESP32 Random Number Generator for LoRa Communication Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: We exploit an ESP32-based random number generator (RNG) on LoRa to secure peer-to-peer (P2P) communication. Employing the built-in ESP32 in LoRa could simplify security system designs with no additional RNG hardware required as the security layer. The random numbers generated are a nonce for the initialization vector setup in AES-CTR to enhance the randomness of the ciphertext. It is found that the generated random numbers pass the National Institute of Standards and Technology statistical test suite. This method provides insight into improving the semantic security of the encrypted message by making unique ciphertexts and using AES-Counter modes and AES-Cipher-based message authentication codes as the two layers of LoRa security to check the authenticity and integrity of the message.

articleTitle: Improved Dye Sensitized Solar Cells Efficiency and Stability Using Co-Sensitization Method of Organic Dyes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: DSSCs have drawn much research attention in recent years as they provide numerous potential advantages, such as high energy conversion efficiency, easy fabrication process, colorful and transparent features, and low manufacturing costs. In this work, we used co-sensitization method to enhance the efficiency and stability of dye sensitized solar cells. The organic XY1B dye was used as a co-sensitizer with organic Y123 dye. The ruthenium-based Z907 dye was used as a reference. The absorption spectra of the co-sensitization dye, XY1B:Y123, are more intense as compared to that of individual dyes, XY1B and Y123. The co-sensitized TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films exhibited broader band in the region of $300-450 \mathrm{~nm}$ and in the region of $525-625 \mathrm{~nm}$. XY1B:Y123 sensitized device achieves the highest performance with an efficiency of 5.47% resulting from highest fill factor (FF), short-circuit current density (Jsc), and open-circuit voltage (Voc) are $57.48 \%, 10.69 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$, and 756.77 mV, respectively. A stability test of the DSSC with various organic dyes and ruthenium dye was conducted in an air atmosphere. The co-sensitized device shows excellent stability. After 30 days, the device efficiency (5.22%) slightly drops by 2.7% relative to initial efficiency (5.36%). In comparison, the device efficiency of ruthenium-based dye Z907 (3.19%) drops by $\mathbf{2 2. 4 \%}$ relative to initial efficiency (4.11%).

articleTitle: UWB Radar Self-Motion Cancelation for Through-Wall Vital Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Through-wall vital sign detection using radar is feasible for search and rescue missions in post-disaster areas. However, the weakness of vital signs makes them easily obscured by noise and clutter. Moreover, even slight random movements of the radar platform can significantly degrade detection accuracy. To mitigate this issue, this paper introduces a technique for detecting and extracting through-wall vital signs in the case of non-stationary radar via sequential image processing. The proposed method targets the detection of life signs using radar mounted on a hovering drone experiencing vertical drift. To replicate this setup, the radar is moved randomly back and forth in front of the barrier/wall and artificial vital sign. The results underscore the efficacy of the proposed method in detecting human respiratory signals.

articleTitle: Optical Fiber Simulation: Corning SMF-28 as a Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) with Optigrating Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study explores how we can transform Corning SMF-28 optical fiber, a common commercial product, into a highly efficient Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensor using simulation techniques. FBG sensors are widely used because of their ability to precisely measure strain and temperature by reflecting specific wavelengths of light. To enhance the sensor’s performance, we applied chirping methods and apodization, which modify the fiber’s structure to improve how it responds under different conditions. Our simulations focused on how different chirp periods, like linear, quadratic, square root, and cubic root, impact the sensor’s sensitivity—especially when it comes to detecting strain and temperature. The results showed that quadratic and square root chirps provided the highest sensitivity, making the sensor more responsive to changes in the environment.

articleTitle: High-Level Synthesis of FPGA-Based Chirp Match Filtering for Synthetic Aperture Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of chirp match filtering for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) using High-Level Synthesis (HLS). HLS enables higher productivity by significantly reducing development time compared to traditional hardware description languages (HDL). A C-based programming approach is employed to leverage parallel processing, which is critical for high-performance signal processing tasks. The design utilizes a symmetric chirp signal as the reference for match filtering, with optimizations implemented through parallelism in the filtering process. Experimental results show that the FPGA-based match filtering, programmed using HLS, achieves low latency and high performance, with a speed increase of 937 times compared to running the same process in Octave on a standard computer.

articleTitle: Impact of Uniaxial Strain Treatment on Thermoelectric Performance of Alkaline-Earth Stannate Oxides: DFT Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Recently, perovskite oxide-based materials, particularly alkaline-earth stannates, have shown promising candidates for thermoelectric applications. However, previous studies mainly concentrated on bulk material rather than thin film. A strategy like band engineering has been used to improve the thin film thermoelectric performance by strain treatment. This study examines the thermoelectric properties of alkalineearth stannate oxides under uniaxial strain using density functional theory (DFT) and Boltzmann transport theory. The results reveal that the tensile strain treatment predominantly improved the electrical conductivity, with BaSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> contributing 6.5 times higher electrical conductivity value under uniaxial strain. Meanwhile, compressive strain enhanced the Seebeck coefficient. Additionally, for CaSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, the Seebeck coefficient results suggest an interplay between charge carriers due to band gap shifting. Power factor improvements were seen between $300-650 \mathrm{~K}$ across all materials. Furthermore, strain generally increased the power factor at above 650 K. The study emphasizes the importance of optimizing strain direction and magnitude to achieve the desired thermoelectric performance enhancement.

articleTitle: The Potential of Silica-Carbon Nanotubes Composite for Electromagnetic Absorber Coating
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The utilization of shielding materials to absorb electromagnetic waves has been widely implemented, especially in military technology and equipment. In this study, we developed a composite material based on silicon dioxide ($\mathbf{S i O}_{2}$) and multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) to enhance the electromagnetic wave absorption compared to single material $\mathbf{S i O}_{2}$. In addition, a marine coating matrix was used in this research. The material characterization was done using scanning electron microscope (SEM) analysis to observe the surface morphology. Meanwhile, a vector network analyzer was used to determine scattering parameters at a frequency range of $4-8 \mathrm{GHz}$ and $8-12 \mathrm{GHz}$. The measurement results showed that the absorber layer of $\mathbf{S i O}_{2} /$ MWCNTs $\mathbf{2 w t} \%$ composite had the highest absorption coefficient of 34.37% at a frequency of 7.66 GHz.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Spatial and Temporal Land Clutter Statistics in SAR Imaging Based on MSTAR Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The statistical analysis of land clutter for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging has become an increasingly important subject for research and investigation. It is also absolutely necessary for designing robust algorithms capable of performing the task of target detection in the background clutter. Any attempt to extract the energy of the desired targets from the land clutter requires complete knowledge of the statistical properties of the background clutter. In this paper, the spatial as well as the temporal characteristics of the land clutter are studied. Since the data for each image has been collected based on a different aspect angle; therefore, the temporal analysis contains variation in the aspect angle. Consequently, the temporal analysis includes the characteristics of the radar cross section with respect to the aspect angle based on which the data has been collected. In order to perform the statistical analysis, several well-known and relevant distributions, namely, Weibull, Log-normal, Gamma, and Rayleigh are considered as prime candidates to model the land clutter. The goodness-of-fittest is based on the Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence metric. The detailed analysis presented in this paper demonstrates that the Weibull distribution is a more accurate fit for the temporal-aspect-angle statistical a nalysis w hile the Rayleigh distribution models the spatial characteristics of the background clutter with higher accuracy. Finally, based on the aforementioned statistical analyses and by utilizing the Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) algorithm, we perform target detection in land clutter. The overall verification of the analysis is performed by exploiting the Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) data-set, which has been collected in spotlight mode at X-band, and the results are presented.

articleTitle: I/Q Imbalance Compensation and Block-Sparsity-Based Harmonic Analysis with Applications to Vital Signs Estimation using CW Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Recently, breathing and heart rate estimation based on radar technologies have become increasingly popular. Millimeter wave radars are compact, low-cost and can perform vital signs estimation without the necessity of having physical contact with the subject under test. However, the strong harmonics of the breathing signal can contaminate the weak heart signal and make the estimation of the heart rate challenging. In this paper, we present the complete theory for vital signs estimation and address two challenging problems in this field, namely In-phase and Quadrature (I/Q) imbalance compensation as well as heart rate estimation in the presence of strong harmonics of the breathing signal. We address the heart rate estimation based on block sparsity model and cast the problem as a convex mixed-integer programming which can be solved efficiently. Finally, we p resent the experimental results gathered from a Continuous Wave (CW) radar operating at 24 GHz. The ground-truth signal to validate the overall accuracy and effectiveness of the algorithms is provided by the Electrocardiogram (ECG) device. Index Terms-I/Q imbalance compensation, block sparsity, breathing and heart rate estimation, convex mixed-integer programming, CW radars.

articleTitle: A Promising Passivation Strategy using Hydroxyethyl Cellulose for Enhancing the Performance of Inorganic-based Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Inorganic perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> have garnered significant attention due to their simple fabrication and excellent stability. However, the presence of interfacial defects within these devices has been reported to hinder their performance. This research presents a novel interfacial engineering approach utilizing hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) as a passivation layer. This study investigates the influence of HEC passivation on the efficiency of CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> based PSC devices comprising FTO/compact$\mathrm{TiO}_{2} /$ mesoporous- $\mathrm{TiO}_{2} / \mathrm{CsPbBr}_{3} /$ carbon. The $\quad$ PSCs performance was analyzed in the presence of HEC, which was deposited either before and after the formation of $\mathbf{C s P b B r}_{3}$ perovskite layer. Optical spectroscopy analysis revealed that HEC modification after perovskite deposition resulted in higher absorption within the visible light range compared to unmodified devices. Furthermore, the PSC constructed by incorporating HEC after CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> deposition exhibited the best performance with PSC constructed by incorporating HEC after CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> deposition exhibited the best performance with an average PCE of $3.06 \pm 0.25 \%$ and an average Voc, Jsc, and FF of $1.29 \pm 0.02 \mathrm{~V}, 4.13 \pm 0.31 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$, and $57.13 \pm 0.50 \%$, respectively. Among PSC devices, the HEC passivated device significantly showed superior properties, wherein the unmodified PSC produced a PCE of $1.27 \pm 0.07 \%$ with a Voc of $0.94 \pm 0.01 \mathrm{~V}$. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy also demonstrated that PSC with HEC deposited after $\mathbf{C s P b B r}{ }_{3}$ layer exhibited a relatively high recombination resistance of $1.42 \times 10^{6}$ ohm. This overall enhancement suggests that the passivation strategy using HEC has effectively suppressed carrier recombination within the CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> layer, thereby leading to improved device performance.

articleTitle: Mobile Adhoc Network (MANET) Protocol Performance with Mobility and Tx Power Variations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A Mobile Ad-hoc network (MANET) is a network consisting of a combination of mobile devices without infrastructure, thus forming a temporary network. Each device has a wireless interface and communicates with each other via radio waves; then, each device is called a node. In a Mobile Ad-hoc Network (MANET), each node can act as a host or a router, so it needs a routing protocol to function. There are three types of routing protocols for Ad-Hoc networks: proactive, reactive, and hybrid. Reactive routing protocols are on-demand, meaning they establish a route from a source node to a destination node only when requested by the source node. Proactive routing protocols are table-driven, where each node maintains a table containing route information to every other node it knows. The route information is periodically updated in case there is a change in the link. The hybrid protocol combines the features of reactive and proactive protocol types. This paper builds upon previous work in this area. The study involves performance testing of MANET protocols like Ad-hoc On-demand Distance Vector (AODV), DestinationSequenced Distance-Vector (DSDV), Dynamic Source Routing (DSR), and Optimized Link State Protocol (OLSR) with varying mobility scenarios and transmitter power on the node to observe changes in network characteristics and their impact on protocol performance. Evaluation is based on the receive rate and packet received. The results indicate that the AODV routing protocol outperforms DSR, DSDV, and OLSR.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Ad-hoc On-demand Distance Vector (AODV) Routing Protocol Using K-Means Clustering in Flying Ad-hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have significant roles across diverse applications, including surveillance, disaster response, search and rescue, etc. Robust communication protocols are crucial in Flying Ad-hoc Networks (FANETs) to maintain reliable connectivity between UAVs. This research examines enhancements to the Ad-hoc On-demand Distance Vector (AODV) protocol by applying the K-Means Clustering method aiming to optimize communication in FANETs. Through extensive simulations in the ns-3 environment, the proposed approach is evaluated in diverse scenarios that consider factors such as node mobility and network density. The results show that integrating AODV with K-Means Clustering improves network Quality of Service metrics, including throughput, packet delivery ratio, and end-to-end delay. This research contributes insights into the feasibility and advantages of employing clustering techniques in FANETs routing protocol.

articleTitle: Deriving Effects of IQ-Imbalance on Phase-and Amplitude Noise in Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The combined effects of local oscillator (LO) phase noise (PN), in-phase / quadrature imbalance (IQI), and range correlation are studied in this paper. We show how PN from an LO appears as PN and amplitude noise (AN) in the received signal of a coherent radar. We derive expressions for the relations between the transmitted signal’s and the received signal’s autocorrelation function (ACF) and power spectral density (PSD) respectively using a first-order Taylor series. The results demonstrate that the PSDs of the PN and AN in the received signal are proportional to the PN-PSD of the transmitted signal. Two coefficients quantifying the PN -scaling and the $\mathbf{P N}$-to-AN conversion are derived as a function of the parameters describing the receiver’s IQI. The derived analytical expressions are compared to the results from MATLAB simulations using a PN PSD typical for a state-of-the-art transceiver. The results demonstrate excellent alignment between theoretical expressions and simulation results.

articleTitle: Enhancing ECG Signal Alignment Accuracy with Smoothed-Quasi-Periodic Dynamic Time Warping
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: An accurate alignment of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for effective diagnosis and classification in healthcare by minimizing the variability due to noise interference, motion artifacts, and individual anatomical or physiological differences. The traditional dynamic time warping (DTW) methods, while commonly used, often struggle with noise and morphological variability in ECG data. This study proposes smoothed-quasi-periodic dynamic time warping (SQP-DTW), a novel approach incorporating a smoothing regularization feature into the quasi-periodic DTW (QP-DTW) framework. Using the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Dataset, we compare SQP-DTW against standard DTW, Shape-DTW, and QP-DTW methods. Our results demonstrate significant enhancements in alignment accuracy in the case of Baseline Wander, Muscle Artifact, and Electrode Motion Noise, evaluated through correlation and percent root difference (PRD). The correlation evaluation shows that QP-DTW and SQP-DTW consistently achieved higher alignment accuracy than standard DTW and ShapeDTW, where SQP-DTW reached a correlation as high as ${0. 9 8}$. Meanwhile, SQP-DTW, particularly under electrode motion noise, performed best, with a percent root difference evaluation of only 20.82 percent. Prospective studies will explore the application of SQP-DTW in real-time ECG monitoring wearable systems and its adaptation to other biomedical signal processing tasks.

articleTitle: PI-Sliding Mode Control on a Hydraulic Dynamometer Test Bed
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A driving environment simulator is an essential system required to develop an electric vehicle. Motor loading test equipment or dynamometers can be used to create driving environment simulators. One common type of dynamometer takes the form of a hydraulic system. In this setup, modifications to the dynamometer loading represent the road resistance. This system, called the Hydraulic Dynamometer Test Bed (HDTB), controls the load change of the motor under test. The controller on the dynamometer is designed to adjust the hydraulic pressure to correspond to road resistance. The hydraulic dynamometer model was developed using an identification system approach involving analyzing non-linear constraints. The torque output and valve opening input data of the dynamometer hydraulic pressure regulator are designed for the model plant. The dynamometer is controlled using the Proportional IntegralSliding Mode Control (PI-SMC) approach to assess and enhance the system’s desired set point accurately. The PI-SMC controller has also been compared with the PID controller to see the improvement of the system response. Implementing the PI-SMC controller on the HDTB increased rise time response performance by $\mathbf{3 0. 7 1 \%}$ compared to using a PID controller.

articleTitle: Impact of Substrate on the SnO2 Electron Transport Layers and the Perovskite Solar Cells Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Developing low-temperature methods for the efficient manufacture of planar perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is crucial for accelerating production and reducing costs. This study investigates the impact of several substrates, specifically fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) and indium tin oxide (ITO), on the deposition of SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers utilized as electron transport layers (ETLs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). The resulting SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers exhibited thinness, conformity, and great transparency, indicating exceptional suitability for PSC applications. Surface characterization by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) demonstrated that FTO substrates consist of bigger merged grains, whereas ITO substrates exhibit smaller grains. The perovskite solar cells constructed on FTO substrates exhibited a greater power conversion efficiency of $\mathbf{1 2. 0 2 \%}$ in comparison to those on ITO, highlighting the advantages of FTO as a substrate in these configurations.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of CSRR-based C-Band Wave Absorber using Evolved Double Split-Ring Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents a performance enhancement of a C-band wave absorber using an evolved double split-ring structure. The C-band wave absorber is developed with the basic shape of a circular patch resonator and ring resonator on an FR4 Epoxy dielectric substrate with a dielectric thickness of 1.60 mm. The performance deficiency of circular patch and ring resonators deals with the structure of open ring resonators, which have better absorption. A double circular split ring resonator (CSRR) with four gaps on each ring resonator is proposed to enhance the performance of the C-band wave absorber, which has an absorption bandwidth of 860 MHz, which, started from 6.54 GHz to 7.40 GHz.

articleTitle: Study of Radiation Pattern Response on Phase-Controlled Ku-Band 8×4 Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the design, simulation, and parametric study of a phase-controlled Ku-Band $8 \times 4$ array antenna for satellite communication. The single element is a rectangular patch antenna fed directly by a $50-0 \mathrm{hm}$ coaxial feed optimized for operation at 12.5 GHz. In the array configuration, 32 elements are arranged linearly along the x and y axes to achieve a gain of 24 dBi. The proposed study focused on the effect of phase control along the x-axis and y-axis to steer the radiation pattern in azimuth and elevation, respectively. Simulations reveal that increasing the phase difference applied to the elements results in a more significant shift of the main beam direction but also increases the sidelobe level (SLL) and decreases the antenna gain. The study further demonstrates that the main beam direction does not increase linearly beyond a specific phase difference, and grating lobes become apparent when the phase difference exceeds 90 degrees. The number of array elements can be increased to achieve a broader range of main beam steering, and higher bit phase shifters can provide finer phase resolution. The findings of this study offer valuable insights for optimizing phase-controlled beam steering in array antennas, balancing performance trade-offs, and enhancing the flexibility and effectiveness of the beam steering mechanism.

articleTitle: Frustum-Shaped Conformal Antenna Array for Air-to-Ground Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this work, a frustum-shaped conformal antenna array for Direct Air-to-Ground Communication (DA2GC) is designed and studied. The requirement calls for an omnidirectional radiation pattern, however the simple monopole or dipole is constrained only to the azimuth plane/yaw and might have deep null in elevation plane due to the aircraft body effect. This work proposes an eight elements conformal array operating at C band frequency covering 4.4 to 5.0 GHz, whose substrate has the shape of a frustum, which provides a solution that meets all the requirements. This design achieves less than 5 dB gain variation across azimuthal coverage and ensures sufficient gain at shallow elevation angles. A passive conformal array on a frustum fed with a microstrip-based $1: 8$ power divider design with results are presented first. Later, an active conformal array with switchable beam is explained. Further, a comprehensive analysis of implementation brought out, indicating that the proposed will be better switchable sectoral coverage is acceptable. This analysis also indicates that the active array configuration requires reduced power due to the increased gain of the array and as it covers only a sector at a given time.

articleTitle: An Extension of Simulating Spanning Tree Protocols in a Dual Landing Station Cable-Based Tsunameter with Multiple Ocean Bottom Units
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Critical networks require some redundancies for their operation. This also applies to INA-CBT, the Indonesia’s cable-based tsunameter. The currently deployed INA-CBT was designed for one landing station (LS) and several ocean-bottom units (OBUs). A prospective way to add extra redundancy is to utilize another LS as a gateway to another data path to the central station. However, this extra LS will cause various spanning tree variations at switching layers. It is important to assess this impact on failover and failback convergence time for ensuring it within the required specification of INA-CBT. This paper aims to investigate the impact of having dual LS to the spanning tree configurations of STP and RSTP protocols in the INA-CBT’s OBU to LS segment by means of simulation using Omnet++. Simulation results in both mesh and ring physical topologies under some possible incident scenarios show that failover and failback time achieved meet the requirements.

articleTitle: Utilization of Partial and Curling Shaped Ground Planes Microstrip Antenna for L-Band Satellite Reception
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Reception of NOAA-19 and Metop-B/C lowresolution optical remote sensing data is carried out at ground stations using L-band frequencies. This research proposes a microstrip antenna combined with a parabolic antenna for $\mathbf{L -}$ band reception. The design of the antenna utilized a combination of truncated and slot techniques on the aperture patch, partial and curling-shaped on ground planes. Measurements showed an impedance bandwidth of 1.02-2.01 $\mathbf{G H z}(\mathbf{9 9 0} \mathrm{MHz}$), an axial ratio bandwidth of $1.45-1.85 \mathrm{GHz}(400$ $\mathbf{M H z}$), and a microstrip antenna gain of $\mathbf{5. 8 3 \mathrm { dB } \text { When paired }}$ with a 1.5 m parabolic reflector, the total system gain reached $\mathbf{2 3. 6} \mathbf{d B}$. These results suggest that the developed antenna could be used as a feed option in ground stations for receiving satellite remote sensing data.

articleTitle: Analysis on Modified Wine Glass Shaped Transparent MIMO Antenna with Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper proposes a 1x2 MIMO (multiple input, multiple output) antenna system that features a modified wine glass-shaped antenna with an I-shaped structure on the top layer and a C-shaped structure on the bottom layer, designed as a double-negative (DNG) metamaterial. The antenna is designed, simulated, and optimized at a frequency of 28 GHz using Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) as the conductive material. Three configurations are explored: parallel MIMO, orthogonal MIMO, and opposite MIMO. The results indicate that the parallel MIMO configuration demonstrates superior performance in terms of isolation and reduced mutual coupling effects. Specifically, the gain of the parallel MIMO configuration reaches 5.9 dBi, while the highest gain of 8 dBi is achieved with the opposite MIMO configuration. These findings suggest that the choice of MIMO configuration significantly impacts the overall performance of the antenna system in 5G applications.

articleTitle: Laser-Powered Extensometer for Soil Displacement Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The Earth’s geological diversity exposes regions to various natural hazards, including earthquakes, landslides, and volcanic eruptions, with soil displacement posing significant risks to infrastructure stability and agricultural productivity. Previous landslide monitoring systems encountered challenges such as data transmission stability and the vulnerability of power supply systems. In response, a soil displacement monitoring system is proposed, integrating extensometer sensors with advanced fiber optic communication technology and a laser-based power system. Extensometer sensors, known for their precise soil displacement measurements, face difficulties in long-distance data transmission, addressed by fiber optic communication offering higher bandwidth and extended transmission distances. The laser-based power system enhances system reliability and efficiency through fiber optics, ensuring uninterrupted operation even in remote locations. System accessibility is further facilitated with a Python-based graphical user interface (GUI) for real-time data visualization. The system’s performance is validated through comprehensive soil displacement simulations, supported by continuous monitoring using a rain simulator to observe potential displacements. This integrated approach, leveraging a robust laser-based power system and advanced communication technology, aims to enhance disaster management strategies in geologically active regions.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Modified Rectangular Array Configurations for Improved Radiation Performance in Ku-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of modified rectangular array configurations aimed at enhancing radiation performance for Ku-band applications. Traditional rectangular arrays, while effective in achieving high gain, often suffer from elevated sidelobe levels, which can lead to interference in sensitive environments. To address this, we investigated several geometric modifications, including square-cut and L-shaped cut arrays, to reduce the number of active elements and improve key performance metrics such as gain, sidelobe level (SLL) and half-power beamwidth (HPBW). The modified arrays were simulated and compared with a conventional $25 \times 25$ rectangular array. The results demonstrate that the square cut array offers balanced performance with a gain of 31.9 dBi and an SLL of - $\mathbf{2 0. 2} \mathrm{dB}$, while the L-shaped cut array significantly reduces sidelobe levels to $\mathbf{- 2 4. 2} \mathbf{d B}$, making it ideal for interference-prone applications. These findings highlight the importance of choosing the appropriate array configuration based on specific application requirements and suggest that further optimization could lead to even greater performance improvements in future antenna systems.

articleTitle: Prototypes of Footstep Voltage Generation on Different Tiles Placement Using Piezoelectric Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Technology advancements in energy harvesting have been sparked by increasing demand for renewable energy sources that are sustainable. This research work outlines the development and experiment of a prototype of piezoelectric voltage generation for energy harvesting from human footsteps. The study addresses the feasibility of generating electricity by converting mechanical energy from the vibrations generated by foot traffic in public areas such as stairs and entrance doors. The objectives of this study are to implement a sustainable and efficient method of generating electricity using piezoelectric materials, explore, and also optimize the mechanical design of the prototype to maximize the conversion of mechanical energy into electrical energy. The proposed system was developed on 2 different devices which are Tile A (25 parallel and 5 series sensor connections) and Tile B (20 parallel and 5 series sensor connections) and tested under different circumstances such as different tile placements, weights, and conditions which are 100, 200, and 300 steps to address the consistency on each predetermined parameter. Furthermore, the final system has the highest voltage generated up to 0.98 V from tile A and 2.54 V from tile B. This is due to the different approach of human footsteps when stepping on stairs and entrance door.

articleTitle: Image Classification-Based Ransomware Attack Detection Using Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Ransomware represents a significant cybersecurity threat that can potentially damage corporate entities. Conventional antivirus methodologies must be revised to mitigate emerging and complex cyber-attack vectors. This study introduces an architecture for a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) predicated on deep learning paradigms; it utilizes a dataset composed of both malicious and benign executables. These files were transformed into grayscale images via the Python Imaging Library (PIL) and subsequently processed by the CNN to effectively discriminate between images indicative of ransomware and those classified as benign. The effectiveness of the CNN model was measured using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and the F1 score. The training accuracy was 0.9476, while the validation accuracy was 0.9383 percent. Moreover, the precision, F1 score, and recall of training were higher than their respective validation rates. This model can contribute to developing an effective solution for detecting ransomware attacks, complement existing approaches, and improve accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of New Traffic System YOLO-LIO: Light-Traffic Intercept and Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Vehicle detection is an area of active development aimed at enhancing driving safety and ensuring compliance with traffic regulations. Despite ongoing efforts, accidents and traffic violations continue to pose significant challenges, leading to disruptions in driving. In response to these issues, the author aims to develop a more efficient traffic management system to improve driver organization and driving behavior. To achieve this, the author proposes using YOLO-LIO as the neural network of choice for the Traffic System. The effectiveness of YOLO-LIO was evaluated using three datasets: the Montevideo Audio and Video Dataset (MAVD), the GARM Road-Traffic Monitoring dataset (GRAM-RTM), and a custom dataset created by the author. The results highlight the superior performance of YOLO-LIO in vehicle detection tasks, achieving accuracy rates of $\mathbf{9 9. 0 2 \%}$ on the MAVD dataset, $\mathbf{9 9. 5 5 \%}$ on the GRAM-RTM dataset, and $\mathbf{9 9. 3 2 \%}$ on the custom dataset. This demonstrates the model’s high effectiveness across various datasets. Additionally, the author conducted experiments incorporating OCR technology with the YOLO-LIO algorithm in the Traffic System. The system achieved an accuracy of $\mathbf{8 0. 2 1 \%}$ in vehicle number detection, demonstrating its effectiveness. This result reflects the overall performance of the entire system process, from data input to the final detection output, ensuring a comprehensive and accurate detection mechanism. Compared to other algorithms such as YOLOv3 + OCR, YOLOv4, and Faster R-CNN, YOLO-LIO + OCR, they have exhibited significantly better performance. These promising results highlight the potential of YOLO-LIO in creating a robust Traffic System that can significantly enhance road safety and traffic regulation compliance.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of SnO2 Deposition Using Spray and Spin-Coating Technique for Electron Transport Layer of Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Organic-inorganic halide perovskites have become notable for their efficiency in light harvesting. Nonetheless, the incorporation of organic cations like $\mathbf{M A}^{+}$and $\mathrm{FA}^{+}$presents stability challenges when exposed to environmental factors. This study explores the potential of replacing organic components with inorganic $\mathrm{Cs}^{+}$to enhance stability and efficiency in PSCs, focusing on CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as the light harvester. We compare spin-coating and spray-coating techniques for depositing SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the electron transport layer, revealing that spray-coating 7 cycles achieves higher PCE. Through detailed characterization, including UV-Vis, FTIR, SEM, I-V, and IPCE analyses, we optimized the manufacture of $\mathrm{SnO}_{2}, \mathrm{CsPbBr}_{3}$, and carbon deposition at room temperature, resulting in a PCE of $\mathbf{2. 2 1 \%}$ using the spray-coating process, demonstrating significant improvements over the spin-coating method.

articleTitle: The Design and Development of LoRa-LoRaWAN Wireless Network Infrastructure with Multi-Hop Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Typically, a wireless mesh network supports multi- hop communication, enhancing data delivery reliability and broader area coverage at a low cost. LoRa, a digital and low- speed communication medium, is not designed to perform these capabilities by default. However, in some conditions, a multi- hop LoRa technology is needed, especially for application in areas with many obstacles and remote areas. To address this issue, this paper discusses designing and implementing a multihop LoRa protocol integrated with LoRaWAN. The multi-hop system increases the success rate of data transmission from the farthest node to the gateway up to $\mathbf{9 4. 0 2 \%}$, which cannot be achieved without multi-hop. In the multi-hop setup, repeater nodes relay the LoRa device signals to subsequent LoRa devices until reaching the gateway. The tests demonstrate how messages flow from the transmitter node to the gateway, which is then forwarded to the LoRaWAN network services without requiring hardware modifications. The tests were conducted indoors under conditions with and without obstacles.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Graphene Oxide-Coated QCM Sensors for Humidity Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study focuses on developing humidity sensors using a quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) coated with graphene oxide (GO) as the sensing layer. The GO was applied to the QCM’s surface electrodes via drop-casting. The performance of the GO-coated QCM was evaluated at varying relative humidity (RH) levels from $\mathbf{4 0 \%}$ to $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ RH, examining key parameters such as sensitivity, hysteresis, response time, and recovery time. The results demonstrated that the GO-coated QCM achieved a sensitivity of $91.06 \mathrm{~Hz} / \% \mathrm{RH}$, with response and recovery times of 77 seconds and 16 seconds, respectively. Characterization of surface morphology, surface area, and functional groups that contain oxygen to the GO material was conducted using XRD, SEM, BET, and FT-IR. Moreover, the study emphasizes the significance of optimal mass depositing for enhancing the sensitivity of QCM sensors.

articleTitle: Unraveling the Interference Puzzle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Factors Contributing to Signal Degradation in Satellite-Based Navigation Systems in the Philippines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study examines various forms of interference affecting Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) in the Philippines, where tropical climates and environmental factors contribute to unique signal degradation challenges. Using data from the Philippine Active Geodetic Station (PAGeNet) network, the research analyzes GNSS data from multiple stations with advanced Python-based tools like PyRINEX for quality checks. Machine learning and statistical methods were applied to identify interference patterns, with a particular focus on cycle slips, ionospheric delays, and multipath effects. The results indicate the occurrence of cycle slips, especially from morning to midday, likely caused by atmospheric changes and satellite handovers. High ionospheric delays are linked to increased electron density, while multipath interference is significantly impacted by environmental factors such as vegetation and buildings. Time series analysis of signal strength reveals correlations with atmospheric conditions, emphasizing the importance of environmental monitoring. The study provides insights into enhancing GNSS robustness using dual-frequency receivers, advanced algorithms, and other tailored mitigation strategies to improve navigation system performance in the region.

articleTitle: The Robustness of Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and Linear Quadratic Regulator Tracker (LQRT) Cascaded With Line-Of-Sight (LOS) Guidance Law for Quadrotor to Accomplish SAR Mission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) algorithm with several patterns is commonly used in quadrotors to examine their capabilities in maintaining positions during search and rescue (SAR) missions. The robustness of conventional LQR and Linear Quadratic Regulator Tracker (LQRT) algorithms cascaded with line-of-sight (LOS) guidance law along a square pattern is compared with and without disturbance and presented in this paper. The systems were analyzed using the root-mean-square error (RMSE) value and time domain response. The results indicate that LQR control without disturbance exhibits a faster response time to reaching the set point, yet it produces a higher overshoot. However, LQRT exhibits a faster settling time and a slight overshoot, while slower in reaching the desired position. Conversely, during the disturbance, LQR control ends with marginally stable for the heave, and the RMSE value remains elevated. Additionally, both end with fluctuated pitch angle position, but LQRT outperforms due to a smaller peak-to-peak deviation. Furthermore, LQRT exhibits a more robust response and stability, with no significant RMSE value change. Therefore, LQRT is the optimal choice for quadrotor utilization in SAR missions and can potentially benefit practitioners, particularly when the mission is under uncertain environment.

articleTitle: Configuration of Hybrid Clustered Structures in Large Planar Arrays for Optimizing Beam Pattern Coverage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Dividing a large planar array aperture (LPAA) into smaller clustered subarrays gives many advantageous in practical implementation of such antenna systems in terms of complexity and cost. In this paper, two new hybrid clustered subarray structures are first proposed to optimize the coverage of the beam patterns (CBP). The hybridization process consists of either 2 by 2 or 4 by 4 clustered subarray structures. The first structure consists of several sub-apertures (i.e., four sub-apertures with 2 by 2 and 16 sub-apertures with 4 by 4), and each sub-aperture is tiled with either irregular clusters or individual radiating elements with specific element excitation amplitudes-only or phases-only. It is also possible that each sub-aperture may contain irregular clusters and individual elements together. The second structure is to hybridize the subapertures with different excitation weights, as each subaperture is fed with an independent excitation of amplitudesonly or phases-only. Then this structure is characterized by hybrid structure and hybrid excitation weights at the same time. Moreover, the thinning technique is included with these hybrid structures to further reduce the array complexity. The process of thinning includes the whole sub-aperture or only a part of it while preserving the characteristics of the original fully optimized CBP such as peak sidelobe level (PSLL) and half power beam width (HPBW). These ideas are implemented through the use of the genetic algorithm (GA) in conjunction with a set of desired constraints such that the required beam pattern coverage can be successfully met. Computational results show that the required CBP can be obtained effectively with the proposed hybrid structures while minimizing the array complexity as small as possible.

articleTitle: Low-SAR Implantable Antennas Design for Small Intestine and Scalp Tissue Phantoms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In Indonesia, a growing population has led to a critical need for biomedical devices to address increasing healthcare demands. Implantable antennas are one of the most important components for Implantable Medical Devices (IMDs) applications used to measure and monitor conditions inside the human body or on its surface. While previous research has designed several implantable antennas, including one for use in endoscopic capsules within the small intestine, the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) was not measured for these designs. SAR is a crucial factor for any wireless communication device implanted in the human body. This research addresses this gap by designing two implantable miniaturized antennas with RT/duroid 6010 substrate and Defected Ground Structure method. The antennas gained SAR values that comply with regulations. The SAR value for the antenna implanted in the scalp phantom is $0.070 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{Kg}$, while the SAR value for the antenna implanted in the small intestine phantom are $\mathbf{0. 0 4 7}$ W/Kg and $0.031 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{Kg}$, all within the ISM Band.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study on Development of D-Shape Polymer Optical Fiber-Based SPR Sensor for Biochemical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR)-based sensing has gained increasing popularity in diverse biochemical contexts, particularly in detecting biomolecular interactions owing to its real-time detection capability and well-established high sensitivity for label-free biomolecule detection. This has led to a rising interest in advancing SPR sensing for swift testing at the point of care. Nevertheless, commercial SPR sensors are inappropriate due to their considerable dimensions, lack of mobility, and elevated expenses. Conversely, utilizing fiber optic-based SPR sensing presents an opportunity to create compact and easily transportable SPR instruments ideally suited for convenient, rapid, and economically viable point-of-care testing. Within this investigation, the researcher conducted an initial exploration to construct an SPR sensor employing polymer optical fiber (POF). In contrast, the refinement of fabrication methods and the deposition of thin gold film thickness were fine-tuned to assess the optical characteristics of the POF-based SPR sensor’s reaction towards alterations in refractive index by utilizing diverse concentrations of glycerin solutions. Out of the array of POF-based SPR sensors manufactured, the most effective sensor displayed a sensitivity measure of $4.585 \pm 0.489$ accompanied by an R-squared coefficient of 0.936, a Limit of Detection (LoD) of 0.31 mM, a stability rate of 63.5%, and a penetration depth of 77.7 nm. These outcomes underscore the capability of the developed POF-based SPR sensor to produce surface plasmon resonance and provide a reliable SPR output in identifying fluctuations in glycerin concentration within the D-shaped sensing component. This investigation sets the stage for developing portable and compact SPR sensors for point-of-care implementations.

articleTitle: Band Stop Frequency Selective Surfaces Using Ring Resonators: Simulation and 6G Metasurface Potential
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive simulation study on the design of a single-layer frequency selective surface (FSS) composed of circular loop or ring resonator unit cells on an F4BMX substrate. The proposed FSS exhibits band stop characteristics with a fractional bandwidth of 76%, centered at 3.5 GHz, and a Q factor of 1,315. The ring resonator has a symmetrical design, which ensures it fits easily in real-world conditions. Full-wave simulations, coupled with parameter sweeping, were conducted to analyze the transmissive and band stop properties based on variations in ring width, outer diameter, substrate thickness, and copper layer thickness. The simulations reveal that a resonant frequency of 3.5 GHz with -50 dB attenuation can be achieved. This work demonstrates how the integration of the ring resonator on an F4BMX substrate can significantly enhance the efficiency, selectivity, and anti-interference capabilities of metasurfaces for advanced communication systems. The work provides insightful information about how to create high-performance, low-cost spatial filtering metasurfaces for next-generation communication such as 6 G.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Pothole Detection and Its Dimension Estimation Using YOLOv8 and Depth Camera for Road Surface Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Pothole detection and dimension estimation are essential to improve the safety and comfort of autonomous vehicles. This paper uses a depth camera to present a new approach for position estimation and pothole detection using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) method. Experimental results on detection applications using real cars show good pothole detection accuracy in both bright and dimly lit road conditions covered by trees with precision. This object detection uses the YOLO version 8 nano model accompanied by coco as pre-trained training. In the training dataset, only one class, namely the pothole dataset, is used. A depth camera from Intel Realsense type D455 will be employed, and the Jetson Orin Nano will subsequently apply the training results. During the field test, data about the position of the pothole coordinate inside the pixel frame, the pothole’s width, and its distance from the camera will be displayed, in addition to pothole-detecting objects. Every pothole object found will have its data shown in real time. Validating the width and length of the pothole involves taking actual measurements with a meter. The estimated distance and width of potholes showed good agreement with direct manual measurements with R -squared values above 0.97 and gradients approaching unity.

articleTitle: Exoskeleton Effects on Amplitude Distribution of Muscle Signals during Oil Palm Fruit Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study investigated the effect of soft exoskeleton on harvesters’ muscle activation. The amplitude probability distribution function (APDF) analysis on surface electromyography (SEMG) data was used to observe the fluctuation of muscle activation during the harvesting task. The measured muscles were biceps brachii, trapezius, and lumbar erector spinae. Five experienced harvesters from a plantation at Tanah Laut Regency participated in this field experiment. They cut the fronds and fruit bunches using a 5 -meter-long pole sickle without and with the soft exoskeleton. The APDF values which indicate the accumulative and variability of muscle activation suggest that the exoskeleton cannot improve the motor control strategy of the harvesters, as further adaptation to the new technology is needed. Combining the APDF approach with other methods is necessary to design a better exoskeleton and harvesting work management.

articleTitle: Analysis of Hybrid Feature and Data Adaptation Techniques for User-Dependent and User-Independent Driver Condition Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Distracted drivers are one cause of many traffic accidents. Therefore, there is a need for a system that can provide warnings to distracted drivers. Many accurate systems have been reported in previous studies, but some systems cannot recognize new users. This research seeks to develop an accurate and robust system to detect driver distraction using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for these conditions to improve the robustness of new drivers. This research proposes hybrid features and retraining with adapted data. Hybrid features combine natural features from RGB color composition with artificial features from Scale Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT). This is called SIBlend. For reference, we use RGB features only. The model, named RGBumble, achieves the best accuracy, but it is not able to recognize new drivers. While SIBlend has lower accuracy, it is more robust when dealing with new drivers. The results of RGBumble mode reaches $\mathbf{98. 50 \%}$ and SIBlend $\mathbf{99. 00 \%}$. The results of RGBumble for new users are the best at $\mathbf{90. 00 \%}$ and SIBlend at 90.4%.

articleTitle: Low-Cost 9.4 GHz Microstrip Patch Antenna Design with PLA and Copper Tape
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The paper presents a low-cost rectangular microstrip patch antenna with a center frequency of 9.4 GHz, using copper tape as the conductive element and polylactic acid (PLA) as the dielectric substrate. This design is intended to create a cost-effective, environmentally friendly, and easily fabricable antenna for radar and communication systems. PLA dielectric substrates are 1.5 mm thick and have a relative permittivity of 2.75 and a loss tangent of 0.017. Antenna simulations in CST Microwave Studio showed an S11 of - ${1 7} \mathrm{d B}$, bandwidth of 503 MHz, and gain of 7.11 dBi.
