It is demonstrated that the antenna operates effectively at the desired frequency, making it suitable for use in radar and wireless communication systems. This study demonstrates that copper tape and PLA, a biodegradable material, can be used to create inexpensive, readily manufactured microstrip patch antennas.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of State and Output Feedback-based Repetitive Controllers for Rotational Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study examines the tracking performance of state and output feedback-based repetitive controllers (RCs) for rotational control systems. First, a state feedback RC is designed in the time domain using a state-space model, which requires full state information for implementation. The state feedback RC is modeled as a 2D hybrid system, where the control and learning actions can be designed independently using Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) solutions. This approach is evaluated on a rotational control system expressed as a strictly proper linear system with a relative degree of 1. Second, for comparison, an output feedback RC, also known as a general RC, is designed for the same system. Numerical experiment results show that while the state feedback RC achieves lower peak and root-means-quare errors, it exhibits slower transient response compared to the output feedback RC.

articleTitle: Rapid and Low-Cost Microfluidic Devices Fabricated Using a 3D Printer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Microfluidic has emerged as a strong tool in several domains, including biology, chemistry, and medicine. However, manufacturing microfluidic devices using traditional techniques such as photolithography and soft lithography may be costly and time-consuming. In this research, we described a low-cost microfluidic device production approach based on a 3D printer. The 3D printer employs digital light precision technology to produce microfluidic devices with extreme precision and accuracy. Using this technology, microfluidic devices are created, showcasing its potential for usage in lab-on-a-chip and sensor applications. Our findings show that the 3D printer can produce high-quality microfluidic devices for a substantially cheaper cost than previous approaches.

articleTitle: Electron Lifetime and Electron Transport Time Determination of The Device With Pt/PW11 Cs/cellulose as Counter Electrode in DyeSensitized Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Platinum is a material commonly used as a counter electrode in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) because of their excellent catalytic performance and electrical conductivity; however, platinum is an expensive material. Some studies have been conducted to modify Pt-based counter electrodes by adding dopant materials with good conductivity and catalytic properties, such as polyoxometalate. In this paper, we utilize polyoxometalate material, PW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>Cs, as a dopant of Pt-based counter electrode. Electron lifetime ($\tau_{e}$) and electron transport time $\left(\tau_{t r}\right)$ of the device with $\mathrm{Pt} / \mathbf{P} W_{11} \mathrm{Cs} /$ cellulose as counter electrode and its control are studied through transient photovoltage (TPV) and photocurrent (TPC) measurements. Electron lifetime ($\tau_{e}$) extracted from TPV shows that the device with $\mathbf{P t} / \mathbf{P} W_{11} \mathbf{C s} /$ cellulose has longer $\tau_{e}$ than its control, indicating a slow recombination process. Electron transport time ($\tau_{\text {tr }}$) extracted from TPC shows that the device with $\mathbf{P t} / \mathbf{P} W_{11} \mathbf{C s} /$ cellulose has $\tau_{\text {tr }}$ faster than its control, indicating that the device with $\mathrm{Pt} / \mathrm{PW}_{11} \mathrm{Cs} /$ cellulose performs better than its control. Both TPV and TPC of the device with Pt/PW11Cs/cellulose show better performance than the control, as shown by the enhancement in power conversion efficiency $(\eta)$ from 3.54 percent (control) to 3.76 percent.

articleTitle: Leveraging Bellhop Model and Multi-Criteria Decision Making for Reliable Underwater Acoustic Link in Marine Buoy System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Due to its long-range capability, the underwater acoustic channel is commonly used as communication link media between the bottom and surface unit in a marine buoy system. However, changes in the sea environment heavily affect the underwater acoustic channels, making them less reliable than radio waves. This problem brings up challenge in determining the optimal distance between the bottom unit and the surface buoy. To address this problem, this paper leverages the Bellhop model to investigate acoustic channel loss characteristics for both uplink and downlink at this particular channel due to varying underwater sound speeds. Once the channel loss characteristics have been obtained, we define a mathematical formulation by using the multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) method to determine the optimal distance between the bottom and surface unit that would offer more reliable acoustic link. The results show that the proposed technique is capable of determining optimal distance for different buoy mooring configurations. We believe that the proposed method will benefit for buoy construction and deployment guideline

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Systolic Array Architecture using 4:2 Compressor Approximate Multiplier for Image Processing Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This research presents an innovative FPGA implementation of a $128 \times 128$ convolution systolic array architecture, optimized for image processing applications. The core of this design is a novel $8 \times 8$ dadda $4: 2$ compressor approximate multiplier, which offers a dynamic balance between computational precision and hardware efficiency. By configuring the systolic array with the multiplier, the design harnesses the inherent parallel processing capabilities of FPGAs to achieve high-throughput performance. The proposed dadda 4:2 compressor approximate multiplier introduces flexibility by enabling the adjustment of computational accuracy according to specific requirements, which is critical for various image processing tasks. This multiplier is integrated into a systolic array architecture, facilitating efficient operations. This architecture is utilized in edge detection of an image. The entire system is described using Verilog HDL and synthesized on the Xilinx Virtex-5 FPGA platform. A comprehensive evaluation is conducted to compare the performance of the dadda 4:2 compressor approximate multiplier against the exact multiplier. Key performance parameters such as area, delay, and power consumption are analyzed in detail. Results from this study indicate that the dadda 4:2 compressor approximate multiplier significantly reduces area (by $\mathbf{2 1. 2 4 \%}$), delay (by 56.95%) and hardware resource utilization without compromising essential computational accuracy. This advancement contributes to the development of adaptive and efficient hardware architectures.

articleTitle: Performance of PVA-SnO2 and PVA-ZnO as Sensing Materials for Thick Film Resistive Type Humidity Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study compares the performance between PVA-SnO2 with PVA-ZnO as a sensitive layer material for resistive humidity sensor. The sensor was fabricated using thick film technology with screen printing method, while the sensitive layer was deposited using spin coating. Electrical resistance testing was carried out in a chamber with a humidity level of 60$\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ RH. Metal oxide as a sensitive layer material varied in mass concentration by 5% and 10% against PVA. The test results show that the F6 PVA-ZnO 5% humidity sensor has a better response with lower resistance of $1.38 \times 10^{7}$ than $\mathrm{PVA-SnO} \mathrm{O}_{2} 5 \%$ of $1.71 \times 10^{7}$ at a relative humidity 60% RH. However, the PVA$\mathrm{SnO}_{2} \mathbf{1 0 \%}$ humidity sensor showed better linearity than PVA$\mathrm{ZnO} \mathbf{1 0 \%}$ over the humidity range tested.

articleTitle: Luminescence Characteristics of Polystyrene-Based Sensor for Gamma-Rays Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The polystyrene-based optical sensor was successfully developed to detect gamma-rays, and it has extensive applications in medical, industrial, and environmental fields. This underscores the importance of thoroughly evaluating the sensor’s performance. The Polystyrene-based optical sensor was constructed using three primary components: polystyrene (derived from styrene monomer) as the matrix, PPO (2,5-Diphenyloxazole) as the fluorescent dye, and POPOP (1,4-Bis(5-phenyloxazol-2-yl) benzene) as the wavelength shifter. The fabrication was carried out using the thermal polymerization method. The sensor’s performance was assessed for its optical and scintillation perspectives. Photoluminescence measurements indicated that commercial and fabricated sensors emit light in the blue region, following similar trends. The pulse height spectra were evaluated using a photomultiplier tube (PMT) targeted by gamma-rays from Cs137. The results showed that the Compton spectrum characteristics of the commercial and fabricated sensors were almost identical, with the light yield being only slightly different: $\mathbf{1 0, 0 0 0}$ photons/MeV for the commercial sensor and $\mathbf{9, 9 8 9}$ photons/MeV for the fabricated sensor. These findings indicate that the fabricated polystyrene-based optical sensor has significant potential for gamma-rays detection, given its performance is comparable to that of commercial sensors.

articleTitle: Innovative Designs for Enhanced Connectivity for 3G and 4G Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Cellular network planning is important for keeping networks fast as demand for mobile services continues growing. The goal of this paper is to plan both a 3G UMTS (Universal Mobile Telecommunications System) network and a 4G LTE (Long Term Evolution) network for Hilla City in Iraq. Analysis were done to design these two networks for that area. 4G technology offers high-speed data and voice services, while 3G technology offers slower data and voice services compared to 4 G technology. It’s worth mentioning that both 3 G and 4 G cellular networks are commonly deployed by different mobile operators in Iraq country. In this study we have used the WiMAP software tool to plan and study the suggested design. Several calculation topics are used to assess the performance of the suggested planning, including elevation calculations, best server, carrier-to-interference ratio, power level, and coverage. In addition, certain customers and nodes are distributed throughout networks to evaluate the coverage, received power levels, and interference at various places within the planned area more precisely. The proposed design covers an area of 80 km2 centered in Hilla city in Iraq country where both UMTS and LTE designs are applied. This paper also discusses a comparative study between the two designs and offers ideas for improvements.

articleTitle: Zirconia Spacer Optimization for Improved Performance in HTL-Free Mesoscopic Perovskite Solar Cells with Carbon Electrode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study focuses on optimizing the spacer layer in mesoscopic perovskite solar cells (MSPSCs) to enhance their performance, specifically in cells using a carbon electrode without hole transport layers (namely HTL-free). Two variations of zirconia-based spacers were investigated: ZrNanoxide ZT/SP and Zr-Nanoxide Z/SP. The photovoltaic measurements demonstrated that MSPSCs with the $\mathbf{Z r}$ Nanoxide ZT/SP spacer achieved a significantly higher power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 1.42%, compared to 0.42% for cells using the Zr -Nanoxide $\mathrm{Z} / \mathbf{S P}$ spacer. The enhanced performance of $\mathbf{Z r}$-Nanoxide ZT/SP was attributed to its favourable surface morphology and small particle size, as evidenced by DektakXT profilometry and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis. These findings underscore the critical urgency of spacer selection in optimizing the efficiency of MSPSCs, with Zr-Nanoxide ZT/SP emerging as the more effective material for boosting cell performance.

articleTitle: Functionalization of Polydopamine on Fiber Optic-based Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance for Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study features functionalization of polydopamine (PDA) on Au nanoparticles-coated fiber optics for biosensor applications, demonstrating both real-time (insitu) and at final stage (ex-situ) monitoring of the PDA polymerization with and without stirring. The measurement was set up in reflectance mode. Light from the halogen light source travels through the fiber optic, exciting a localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of the Au nanoparticles along the sensing area in coupling to the evanescence field of the fiber optic. The reflected light spectrum is recorded and monitored by the spectrometer, and the evolution of the LSPR peak is tracked in real-time. As a result, the polymerization and deposition process of the PDA layer on the Au nanoparticle is observed to induce a redshift to the LSPR peak shift due to an increase in PDA thickness and refractive index. Moreover, the implementation of stirring during the PDA deposition process significantly accelerates the polymerization rate. Finally, the PDA functionalization was verified using bovine serum albumin (BSA) adsorption. The real-time binding process of BSA on the PDA layer is indicated by further LSPR peak redshift. The binding of BSA is irreversible upon solvent flush. These results showed that implementation of in-situ monitoring opens the possibility of monitoring nanoscale growth and activity in controlled environment that will benefit the development of sensitive, specific, and real-time biosensors for medical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and food safety applications.

articleTitle: Initial Research to Predict The Length and Weight of Nile Tilapia Using ImageAI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: One of the processes of cultivating Nile Tilapia requires measuring the mass and size of the fish. These measurements are carried out manually, which triggers stress, affects fish growth, and produces fish of lower quality. This system was created to help farmers improve the quality of fish growth rates. Initial research on the fish length and weight prediction system that has been designed goes through several stages, namely collecting actual fish length and weight data, collecting fish image datasets, labeling fish object datasets, and training fish objects with a dataset of 993 images using the ImageAI library, which compares the performance between the two architectures used, namely YOLO (You Only Look Once) V3 and Tiny YOLO V3. The result is that the speed of the Tiny YOLO V3 training process is around 14 hours faster than YOLO V3 around 52 hours. However, the detection results from YOLO V3 have better accuracy, namely 93 percent of the 15 datasets tested, than Tiny YOLO V3, which is only 80 percent. The fish image dataset was taken with a distance between the table and the camera, namely 33 cm. Measuring the length and weight of the fish with the height and width of the fish image pixels has a relationship, namely the longer and wider the fish, the longer and wider the fish image pixel size will be if the detection results are accurate. The conclusion is that the YOLO V3 architecture was chosen to be used for detecting fish objects; apart from that, there are results of Nile Tilapia growth patterns from the formulation of the actual relationship between the length and weight of the fish. There are also height and width values for the image resulting from pixel measurements of the fish image. Thus making this initial research valid and can be continued to complete the research of predicting the length and weight of fish automatically by creating a calculation formula.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-Efficient Image Transmission in Autonomous Vehicles Using Super-Resolution Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The rapid advancement in autonomous vehicle technology promises significant improvements in driving efficiency, safety, and comfort. A crucial aspect of these systems is the real-time processing of visual data to ensure accurate object identification and environmental awareness. However, transmitting high-resolution visual data from vehicles to central server encounters challenges due to bandwidth limitations and network latency. Super-resolution methods, leveraging machine learning, present a viable solution by enhancing image resolution without increasing data transmission bandwidth. This study explores the application of super-resolution techniques for bandwidth optimization in image transmission within autonomous vehicles. By transmitting lower resolution images and enhancing them upon reception, the system reduces network load, ensuring efficient data transfer. The analysis demonstrates the trade-off between image quality and transmission efficiency, emphasizing the potential of super-resolution in bandwidth-limited environments. Implementing the SRCNN architecture shows promising results in maintaining image quality with minimal bandwidth usage, contributing to the development of more efficient and reliable autonomous vehicle systems.
